summary: The first thing in the record here is from December 1906: the United Refugees asking leave to put cottages on the unbuilt parts of Grove Street between Masonic and Clayton. Lowell High School came next — a site chosen in 1909, the land bought that year, the building ordered in 1910 for the block bounded by Grove, Hayes, Ashbury and Masonic. North of it lay the Odd Fellows Cemetery, and once that was gone the streets went in over the ground: Anza Street was cut through to St. Rose's Avenue in 1935 for $40,000, St. Rose's itself was renamed Anza the same year, and Rossi Avenue, Almaden Court, Loraine Court and a row of terraces were taken in as public streets in the years after. Stanyan Street was extended north to Turk in 1931; the following year twenty-five feet of it was closed again and deeded to two women who had paid $3,000 for the ground. Between times the ordinary business went on — forty horses at 506 Stanyan Street in 1914, arc lamps put up a corner at a time, fuel-oil tanks under the flats until about 1931 — and in 1909 Mrs. C. Nichols was given the floor to speak against a police station and stables on Stanyan Street. From the 1980s the Board was mostly being asked to let one building become something else — a private school at 350 Masonic Avenue argued over through 1985 and 1986, a twenty-person care home at 212-214 Ashbury Street in 1993, after which it urged the Planning Commission to set up a neighbourhood committee to watch the conditions. Through all of it the university has been the constant: steam and electric lines run under Parker Avenue for it in 1986, the south side of Anza Street rebuilt for its Lone Mountain campus in 1997, and Loyola Village's flats mapped in 2001.
